issues.t: Oil sludge and oil starvation
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers or comes on, the engine knocks or ticks, or it suddenly loses power. In bad cases the engine seizes with little warning.
issues.why: On the early turbo four-cylinders, long oil-change intervals let sludge and carbon build up and clog the screen on the oil pickup in the pan. Heat from the nearby catalytic converter is thought to cook the oil. The oil light often only comes on once pressure is already gone.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. On any car from these years, have a shop drop the oil pan and clean the pickup if the history is unknown, then change synthetic oil about every 5,000 miles.

issues.t: Ignition module can overheat and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine misfires, runs rough or stalls while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: A transistor inside the ignition discharge module (the ignition cassette that sits on top of the spark plugs) can overheat and burn out. Saab recalled modules built before a certain production change on these engines.
issues.next: Have a Saab-knowledgeable shop or GM dealer check the module date code and whether the recall was done. A failing cassette is a common cause of misfires on these engines either way.

issues.t: Timing chain or balance shaft chain rattle
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter from the front of the engine, often worst on a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light or a new vibration.
issues.why: The timing chain and the separate balance shaft chain wear out faster when the oil is dirty or sludged. Tensioners and plastic guides can break, and a broken guide can damage other parts.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new rattle. Have the chains, guides and tensioner inspected; a chain that jumps a tooth can cause serious engine damage. Keep oil changes short and on schedule.

issues.t: Worn intake valves causing hard cold starts and misfires
issues.sym: Long cranking or no start in cold weather, a rough idle and misfire codes when cold, and the engine smoothing out once warm. Fuel economy may drop.
issues.why: The intake valves on the 2.0T wear and stop sealing, so one or more cylinders lose compression. Owners and shops report this from roughly 55,000 miles onward.
issues.next: Ask for a compression or leak-down test before replacing coils, plugs or sensors. If compression is low, the fix is a valve job on the cylinder head.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil leak or failure
issues.sym: Blue smoke on start-up, oil use between changes, a whistle or loss of boost, or oil around the turbo pipes.
issues.why: Turbo seals wear, and a blocked oil return line or a leaking oil feed pipe can starve or flood the turbo. Sludged oil speeds this up.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. Have the turbo, its oil lines and the crankcase ventilation checked before the turbo fails completely.

issues.t: Crankcase ventilation (PCV) failure causing oil leaks and smoke
issues.sym: Oil leaks from seals and gaskets, oily residue, smoke from the engine bay or tailpipe, and in some cases sludge.
issues.why: Clogged or broken crankcase ventilation hoses and valves let pressure build inside the engine. Saab issued updated ventilation parts for these engines.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check the PCV hoses, check valves and drain box, and install the updated parts if they were never done.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the car, a sweet smell, the low-coolant warning, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out. Owners report leaking pumps on both the 2.0T and 2.8 V6 from about 40,000 to 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak traced. Replace the pump before it overheats the engine.

issues.t: Coolant loss from cracked reservoir or hoses
issues.sym: The low-coolant warning comes on again and again, sometimes with no visible puddle.
issues.why: Expansion tanks crack, turbo coolant hoses leak, and on some V6 engines leaks have been traced to the cylinder heads. Some 2.0L engines lose coolant with no clear cause.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Don't keep topping up for months, because running low can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil level sensor
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the bottom of the oil pan, small drips under the engine.
issues.why: The seal on the oil level sensor in the oil pan leaks.
issues.next: Have a shop replace the sensor seal. It is a small job, but keep an eye on the oil level until it is done.

issues.t: Thermostat stuck open
issues.sym: The temperature gauge stays low, the heater is weak, and a check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks partly open so the engine never reaches its normal temperature.
issues.next: Replace the thermostat. An engine that runs cold wastes fuel and wears faster.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure causing misfire
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, shaking at idle and loss of power.
issues.why: Individual coils fail on both the 2.0T and the 2.8 V6. On the V6, the coil closest to the turbo sees the most heat, and corroded connectors can mimic a bad coil.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find which cylinder. Check the wiring connector before buying several coils.

issues.t: Steering column module (CIM) failure
issues.sym: Turn signals stick on or work only sometimes, steering wheel controls stop working, alarm problems, or the car won't start.
issues.why: The column integration module behind the steering wheel, which handles the signals, wipers and part of the anti-theft system, fails.
issues.next: Have the module diagnosed with a Saab scan tool. A replacement module has to be programmed to the car.

issues.t: Key fob or key chip failure
issues.sym: The remote stops locking or unlocking, the alarm goes off when you use the key, or the car won't recognize the key and won't start.
issues.why: The electronic key or its chip fails. Replacing it means buying a new key and programming it to the car.
issues.next: Try a new battery in the fob first. If the key still isn't recognized, a dealer or Saab specialist must program a new one.

issues.t: Power windows reopening slightly after closing
issues.sym: A window goes all the way up, then drops back down about two inches by itself.
issues.why: The anti-pinch function thinks it has met an obstruction, often because the window has lost its learned top position or the glass channel is binding.
issues.next: A shop can re-learn the window positions and adjust the glass. It's usually a quick fix.

issues.t: Power window regulator or motor failure
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, makes grinding or clicking noises, or won't move at all.
issues.why: Window regulators and motors wear out on these cars.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed to see whether the motor, regulator or switch has failed.

issues.t: A/C compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or cuts in and out.
issues.why: Compressor failures were common on 2001-2002 cars, and later owners also report failed compressors. GM issued a bulletin for warm A/C on later cars.
issues.next: Have the system pressures checked before recharging. If the compressor has failed, the system should be flushed when it is replaced.

issues.t: Broken heater air-direction control shaft
issues.sym: Turning the air-direction knob does nothing, so air won't switch between face, feet and windshield.
issues.why: A plastic telescopic shaft behind the dash breaks after repeated flexing.
issues.next: The replacement shaft is inexpensive and can be reached from the side of the center console.

issues.t: Steering rack mount cracking the firewall
issues.sym: Creaks from the steering, a loose or vague steering feel.
issues.why: The steering rack bolts to the firewall, which flexes and can crack around the mounting points over time.
issues.next: Have the rack mounting points inspected. Cracks are repaired by welding or a reinforcing brace.

issues.t: Information display (SID) missing pixels
issues.sym: Letters and numbers on the dash information display fade or have missing lines, making messages hard to read.
issues.why: The small LCD screen in the Saab Information Display wears out.
issues.next: Only the LCD needs replacing, not the whole unit. Saab specialists and DIY kits handle this.

issues.t: Fuel pump or fuel gauge sender failure
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, stalls on the road, or the fuel gauge reads wrong.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump or the fuel level sender fails. GM issued a bulletin on diagnosing pump and gauge faults.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. Don't run the tank very low if the gauge is unreliable.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal sensor codes and reduced power
issues.sym: Check engine light and the car goes into reduced power mode.
issues.why: The ECM sets accelerator pedal position sensor codes (P2122, P2123, P2138 and similar). GM issued a bulletin for these on 2003-2009 Saabs.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pedal sensor and wiring checked.

issues.t: Broken coil spring
issues.sym: A clunk or bang over bumps, the car sitting lower at one corner, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Gravel trapped between the coil spring and its seat wears the coating so the spring rusts and snaps. GM issued a bulletin on this.
issues.next: Replace broken springs promptly, ideally in pairs. A broken spring can cut a tire.

issues.t: Worn stabilizer bar end links
issues.sym: Knocking or rattling from the front over small bumps.
issues.why: The end links and bushings for the stabilizer (sway) bar wear out. It's one of the most-reported repairs on the 9-3.
issues.next: An inexpensive repair; replace both sides.

issues.t: Convertible top stops working
issues.sym: The soft top won't open or close, or stops partway.
issues.why: The soft-top control module can receive invalid signals. Sensors, hydraulics and switches can also fault.
issues.next: Don't force the top. Have the soft-top system scanned; a bulletin covers the control module fault.

issues.t: Sunroof binding, noise or water leak
issues.sym: The sunroof stops, reverses on its own, makes noise or lets water in.
issues.why: Pinch-protection software, the wind deflector and clogged drains cause trouble. Saab and GM issued bulletins.
issues.next: Clear the drains and ask about the software update.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the danger is metal fragments if the airbag deploys.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag inflator can rupture from excess pressure.
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA's recall site and have the free inflator replacement done.

issues.t: Fuel pump may seize and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or won't start.
issues.why: Some fuel pumps were built with the wrong internal parts and can seize.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the pump replaced free.

issues.t: Fuel lines at the pump can loosen and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or a fuel leak under the rear of the car.
issues.why: Fuel pump retaining tabs were damaged in production, so the fuel lines can loosen. Saab added a securing bracket.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel. Check the recall status with a dealer.

issues.t: Brake booster check valve can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly gets hard and the car needs much more pedal force to stop.
issues.why: Heat can damage the vacuum check valve for the brake booster, cutting power assist.
issues.next: Get the recall status checked; a redesigned check valve is installed free.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not retract on sedans (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt stays loose and won't wind back in.
issues.why: The retractor can be damaged in manufacturing and its cable may break.
issues.next: Have the free retractor replacement done.

issues.t: Convertible driver seat belt may not retract (recall)
issues.sym: On the convertible, the driver's belt stays loose and won't retract.
issues.why: The driver's front seat belt retractor can break.
issues.next: Have the free retractor replacement done. The passenger side has lifetime special coverage.

issues.t: Front seatback may fold forward in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the risk is in a frontal crash.
issues.why: The front seat backrest lock may be installed wrong.
issues.next: Have the dealer check recall completion.
